translation.title: Aciclovir Cream
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for herpes simplex virus infections, including initial and recurrent genital herpes and cold sores (herpes labialis), which cause blisters.
translation.usage: Apply to the affected area 5 times a day at intervals of about 4 hours. Continue treatment for 5 days; if it has not healed after 5 days of use, you may use it for 5 more days.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it, if you are breastfeeding, or in children. Before using it, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have an immune deficiency such as AIDS or have had a bone marrow transplant, if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or if you are hypersensitive to or have reacted to propylene glycol. Start treatment as early as possible; for recurrent cases, start when prodromal symptoms or the lesion first appear. Follow the prescribed directions and dosage. Do not use this medicine to prevent transmission to others or to prevent recurrent herpes simplex (blister) infection. Do not use it as a base for diluting or mixing other medicines. This medicine is for external use only. Do not use it on the eyes, cornea, or mucous membranes. To keep the medicine from spreading to other parts of the body or infecting others, apply it while wearing a finger cot or rubber glove. Stop use and consult a doctor or pharmacist if adverse reactions occur, such as discomfort like tenderness, a temporary burning sensation, mild pain including stinging, contact dermatitis, an erythematous rash, eczema, allergic reactions, and at times irritation at the application site, itching, vulvitis, facial swelling, skin discoloration, hives, a rash, a vesicular rash, or skin peeling.
